finding.claim: Unauthenticated path traversal in /dl lets any caller read arbitrary files readable by the service user (e.g. /etc/passwd, secrets, keys) via ../ sequences in the f query parameter.
finding.source: Query parameter 'f' on GET /dl, read at files.go:12 with r.URL.Query().Get("f"); no authentication required.
finding.sink: os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(root, name)) at files.go:13, response written at files.go:18.

trace.note: Attacker-controlled f read from the query string; Query() URL-decodes it, so %2e%2e%2f is equivalent to ../.
filepath.Join calls Clean, which collapses .. segments: f=../../etc/passwd resolves to /etc/passwd. os.ReadFile reads it with no size cap.
Error path returns 404 only when the read fails; it does not block traversal.
Full file contents written to the response.
/dl is registered with no middleware or auth.

finding.guards_checked: None on the path: no filepath.Clean plus prefix check, no filepath.Rel containment check, no strings.HasPrefix against root, no allowlist, no authentication. The only branch (files.go:14-17) returns 404 and does not stop traversal. Not executed; based on documented filepath.Join/Clean semantics. A non-EOF character device would also cause unbounded memory growth via os.ReadFile.

verdict.guard_found: none. The only branch (files.go:14-17) returns 404 on read error and does not stop traversal. No filepath.Clean/Rel or HasPrefix containment check, no allowlist, and no auth middleware; /dl is registered bare at files.go:32. The avatar handler's filepath.Base (files.go:22) is not on the /dl path.
verdict.reason: The attacker is anonymous, and `filepath.Join(root, name)` at files.go:13 cleans `../` segments, so `f=../../etc/passwd` resolves to `/etc/passwd`. `os.ReadFile` at files.go:13 then reads it and `w.Write(data)` at files.go:18 returns the full contents, with no containment check anywhere on the path.

finding.claim: The /dl and /avatar endpoints perform no authentication or ownership check, so any network client that can reach port 8082 can download any file under /srv/files. Severity depends on whether /srv/files holds private per-user content.
finding.source: Any unauthenticated HTTP client reaching the listener on :8082 (bound to all interfaces at files.go:34).
finding.sink: download handler serves any file under /srv/files (files.go:11-19), registered at files.go:32.

trace.note: http.ListenAndServe(":8082", nil) binds all interfaces over plain HTTP with no TLS.
/dl registered on the default mux with no auth wrapper.
Any caller-supplied f is accepted with no identity check.
File contents returned to the unauthenticated caller.

finding.guards_checked: No auth middleware, no per-user ownership check, no TLS. Intent is unknown from this code: if the directory is meant to be public, this is by design and not a defect on its own.

verdict.guard_found: none. No auth middleware or ownership check wraps /dl (files.go:32) or /avatar (files.go:33). The only control is filepath.Base at files.go:22, which applies to the avatar endpoint's u parameter only, not to download's f parameter.
verdict.reason: Anonymous clients reach the unauthenticated plain-HTTP listener on all interfaces (files.go:34), and download() at files.go:12-18 reads whatever f names with no check. The claim understates the scope: filepath.Join(root, name) at files.go:13 cleans the path, so ../ sequences escape /srv/files and any file the process can read is returned, not only files under it. The "by design" caveat does not hold, because the avatar handler's filepath.Base at files.go:22 shows the code intends to contain paths, and download has no equivalent.
